confirmed.title: A returning monster blocked by the river stays in 'return' for good: it can't be damaged, isn't healed and never acquires again (start-town goblin reproduced)
confirmed.evidence: The 'return' branch moves straight home through moveWithCollision. Unlike 'chase', it has no stall check and no other way out. The only exit is dist <= 1.0. I ran the real stepMonster and CAMPS (bundled with esbuild, scratch sim3.ts). A goblin homed at (12,4) in camp three_kettle is hit once (hp 7/8) and chases the player across the bridge. The player walks (6 u/s) along (22,0) -> (36,0) -> (37,5) and then east. The trace: 4.78s chase -> return at (35.37,3.00). After 40 s it is still 'return' at (33.89,3.25) with hp 7/8, and onPlayerHit(...).applied is false. A random-walk lure sweep over every camp member (5400 runs) left 10 monsters stuck the same way, all three_kettle goblins on the east bank next to the bridge.
confirmed.scenario: A new player in Lumbridge hits a passive goblin and runs over the bridge and up the east bank. The leash fires off the bridge deck. The straight line home runs into deep water: the full move and the x-only move are both blocked, and the z-only component dies out at z≈home z. The goblin stands at the shore forever. Every hit shows 'has lost interest', it never heals or resets, and the player can't kill it until a reload. This breaks T6: return must end at home.
confirmed.fix: Give 'return' the same stall test as 'chase'. Keep decrementing stallTimer, and if the monster has moved less than 0.2 in 1.5 s, snap it to (homeX, homeZ) and apply T6 (full HP, breathCount 0, 'reset'). A simpler alternative is a return timeout that teleports it home. Add a G2.4 test with the bridge lure above.

check.reason: The finding holds. In src/state/monsterAi.ts:131-146 the 'return' branch only steps straight toward home with moveWithCollision. It has no stall check and no timeout, and the only way out is dist <= 1.0. The engine (src/engine/loop.ts:636) just copies the position, and onPlayerHit (line 255) rejects every hit while the monster is in 'return'. moveWithCollision (src/state/collision.ts:97-105) tries the full move, then x only, then z only. When the leash fires just east of the river at z≈3, outside the bridge deck (|z| <= 2.05), the move west runs into deep water (isDeepWater). The z-only step then pushes the goblin toward home z=4, which takes it further from the bridge, so it never gets back across. I reproduced it with my own sim at /tmp/claude-1000/-home-rdrosa-gitprojects-allan-osrs-like/49c111c4-413d-4c3a-9eed-67685c0d7161/scratchpad/sim.ts, bundled with esbuild and run against the real stepMonster and CAMPS. A goblin homed at (12,4) in three_kettle is hit once and chases the player along (22,0) -> (36,0) -> (37,5) -> east. It switches to return at 5.23 s at (35.21,2.77). At 50 s it is still 'return' at (33.74,2.85) with hp 7, and onPlayerHit(...).applied is false. It happens in ordinary early play (start-town goblin, the main bridge), and that one monster stays invulnerable and stuck until the page reloads. No data is lost or corrupted, and the rest of the world is unaffected, so medium is the right severity.

confirmed.title: The hero gets stuck against water or walls: for resource and station targets the last segment aims at the entity, not at the planned goal cell
confirmed.evidence: `if (player.waypoints.length > 1) { aim = waypoints[0] } else { aim = targetVec }`. Once only the goal waypoint is left, the player steers straight at the entity (a fishing spot sits in deep water). The goal waypoint is never reached, so it is never shifted. Re-pathing only exists for monsters, so nothing recovers. I mirrored this loop logic over every NODE_PLACEMENTS node, starting from 48 points around each (scratch sim.ts): 78 of 2003 approaches never reached stop distance 3.1. Example: shrimp spot (27,5) approached from (27,11). The path is [[25.5,7.5]], but the player aims due south at (27,5), hits water at (27,9.37) with dx=0, and moveWithCollision returns the same position every frame. Spot (27,-8) gives the same result from 5 starts. The spec (6.7) says the path ends at a walkable goal within stop distance, and only the monster case aims at the target between re-paths.
confirmed.scenario: A player standing north of a Lumbridge shrimp spot clicks it. The hero runs in place at the riverbank and never fishes, until the player clicks somewhere else. The same aim rule applies to monster targets: a still monster across water or a wall leaves the hero stuck until the monster moves 2 units.
confirmed.fix: For resource and interactive targets, keep aiming at the last waypoint: use `player.waypoints.length > (target.type === 'monster' ? 1 : 0)`. For monsters, also re-path, or fall back to the waypoint, when the player made no progress over a short window.

check.reason: The finding is real and I could not refute it. In src/engine/loop.ts:259-265, once only one waypoint is left the hero steers straight at the entity (targetVec), not at the planned goal cell. moveWithCollision (src/state/collision.ts:97) returns the same position when both axis moves are blocked. The only re-path is the monster branch (shouldRepath), so resource and interactive targets have no way to recover. I mirrored the loop with the real buildWalkGrid, entityGoal, findPath and moveWithCollision in a temporary vitest file, which I deleted afterwards (git status is clean). Approaching the shrimp spot at (27,5) from (27,11) gives the path [[25.5,7.5]], and the hero stops at (27.00, 9.40), 4.40 from the spot, so stop distance 3.1 is never reached and it never fishes. This matches the reviewer's numbers. A second case, spot (27,-8) approached from (27,-2), also stalls at about 5.99. The monster version holds too: when the hero is stuck on the last leg, waypoints is not empty, so reachedLast is false, and a monster that stays still never moves the 2 units shouldRepath needs, so no re-path happens. Medium fits. Common gathering and combat clicks silently fail from some approach angles, but nothing crashes or corrupts data, and the player can get out by clicking somewhere else.

confirmed.title: Attacking a returning (immune) monster still uses up runes, arrows and special energy every tick, and prints the 'lost interest' line each time
confirmed.evidence: performPlayerAttack calls prepareAttack and `prep.consume.forEach(cost => removeItem(...))` (and drains spec energy) before applyDamage runs onPlayerHit. onPlayerHit returns applied:false for state 'return', and the code then only shows a miss and `The X has lost interest.`. targetEntity is not cleared, so updatePlayerIntent attacks again every TICK_SEC (0.6 s) and follows the monster home. Spec 6.5 describes immunity as 'a check in front of the unchanged attack formula' with one chat line.
confirmed.scenario: A ranged or magic player attacks a monster that leashes. While it walks the ~15-20 units home at 5.2 u/s (about 3-4 s), the player auto-fires about 6 times. Each shot spends one arrow or one set of runes (or an armed special) for nothing and adds another chat line, and the player chases it back into its camp.
confirmed.fix: At the top of performPlayerAttack, if monster.logic.state === 'return', show the lost-interest line once, set player.targetEntity = null, and return before prepareAttack and spending anything. Keep the check in onPlayerHit for projectiles already in flight.

check.reason: The finding holds up. In src/engine/actions.ts, performPlayerAttack calls prepareAttack and removes the items in prep.consume (line 91), and it takes special energy when a special is armed (line 133), all before applyDamage runs. In src/state/monsterAi.ts, onPlayerHit returns applied:false when the monster's state is 'return' (line 255). applyDamage then only shows a miss splat and adds "The X has lost interest." (actions.ts:180-183), and it never clears player.targetEntity. In src/engine/loop.ts, the targeting code drops a monster target only when isDown is true (line 170), and a returning monster is not down. So the player keeps walking toward or staying in range of the monster and attacks again every TICK_SEC (0.6 s; loop.ts:226-227), until the monster gets home and goes back to 'idle' with full HP. Every one of those attacks spends ammo or runes, plus special energy if a special is armed, and adds another chat line. The return state starts on leash, on the player being too far, on a stall, or on the player being in a safe zone, so this happens in normal play. Severity stays low. The waste is a few arrows or runes and some chat spam, the monster heals to full at home anyway, and nothing crashes or corrupts state. The fix is to clear the target, or skip the attack before any cost is spent, when the monster is in 'return'.

confirmed.title: Clicking walkable ground is refused when that point's 1-unit cell centre is unwalkable (for example the edge of the bridge deck)
confirmed.evidence: Ground clicks now go through planWalk -> findPath, which returns null when grid.cells[targetCell] === 0, even if the clicked point is walkable. Before this stage the check was isWalkable(pt). Verified (scratch sim4.ts): isWalkable(29, 2.03) is true (bridge deck, |z|<=2.05), but findPath(grid,[0.5,5.5],[29,2.03]) is null because the cell centre (29.5,2.5) is deep water. (29,1.9) is found.
confirmed.scenario: A player clicks the outer strip of the bridge, or the strip of walkable ground at a shoreline or wall face whose cell centre is blocked, and gets 'You cannot walk there.' on ground that was clickable before this stage.
confirmed.fix: When the target cell is blocked but isWalkable(to) is true, path to the nearest open cell, using the same 9x9 search that pathStart uses, and append the exact clicked point as the final waypoint.

check.reason: The finding holds up. On main, a ground click (input.ts:400, and also the 'Walk here' option at about line 347) was accepted whenever isWalkable(pt) was true. Now it goes through planWalk, which calls findPath (src/state/pathfind.ts). findPath floors the target to a 1-unit cell and returns null when grid.cells[targetId] === 0. buildWalkGrid fills each cell by sampling only its centre (origin+g+0.5). So if the clicked point is walkable but its cell centre is not, the player now gets 'You cannot walk there.' The bridge case checks out: collision.ts:37 makes the deck walkable for |z|<=2.05 with x in [20.5,35.5], so a click at z in [2,2.05] lands in the cell centred at z=2.5, which is water. The effect is cosmetic and small. The bridge strip is only 0.05 units wide. Along shorelines and walls the dead strip is at most about half a cell. The player can click a little further in, and walkable ground is not lost for movement. Low severity is right.

confirmed.title: Minimap draws Harrowback Ridge solid across Cinderstep Pass, hiding the only way through
confirmed.evidence: The ridge loop draws every point of `ridge.points` as one continuous 8 px stroke and never reads `ridge.gaps`. The gap at (-32, 55) lies on the segment (-32, 38)-(-32, 124), so the stroke runs straight over it. Paths are drawn first (line 64), so this ridge stroke also covers Cinder Stair where it crosses the pass. Nothing else on the minimap marks the gap.
confirmed.scenario: A player near Wardstone Cairn looks at the minimap. Cinder Stair runs into an unbroken dark wall and there is no pass to see. The minimap tells them the volcanic corner is sealed, which is the opposite of what G2.5 and design 6.10 intend.
confirmed.fix: Leave the gap out of the ridge stroke. Sample each ridge segment, for example once per unit, and start a new sub-path wherever `gapDistance(ridge, qx, qz) <= 0` (from collision.ts). A simpler alternative is to draw the paths after the ridges so that Cinder Stair shows on top of the wall.

check.reason:
The finding is real. I'm rating it low, not medium.

**What the code does.** In `src/engine/overlay.ts`, lines 78-90 (added in commit e9edb2a, W7), the ridge loop draws every point in `ridge.points` as one 8 px stroke in `#1c1917`. It never reads `ridge.gaps`.

**Why the gap is covered.** In `src/data/worldMap.ts`:
- Lines 86-90: Harrowback Ridge has points (-32, 38) and (-32, 124), and its only gap is at (-32, 55) with half-width 2.5.
- The gap therefore sits on that straight segment.
- At minimap scale 1.75, the gap is about 8.75 px wide and the ridge stroke is 8 px, so the stroke covers almost all of it.

**Why the path is hidden too.** Cinder Stair (line 77) runs along z=55 from x=-14 to x=-46, so it crosses the ridge at (-32, 55). Paths are drawn first (line 64) and are 3.6 × 1.75 ≈ 6.3 px wide, so the 8 px ridge stroke drawn afterwards covers the path completely at the crossing.

**Nothing else marks the gap.** `renderMinimap` does not draw POIs. The only shapes drawn there are resource nodes, NPCs and monsters, and the Cinderstep Pass sentries show only as monster dots.

**Why low, not medium.**
- It is a display problem only. Collision (`src/state/collision.ts:69`) does honour the gaps, so the pass can still be walked.
- In the 3D world the gap is visible, marked by two obsidian spires, and Cinder Stair leads straight to it. A player following the road reaches the pass anyway.
- Design 6.10 says only "ridges as dark strokes" and says nothing about drawing gaps. So "the opposite of what 6.10 intends" overstates it; the conflict is with the intent of G2.5 (one visible pass).
- The fix is small: split the stroke at each gap.

check.reason: I could not refute this finding, and the code confirms it. buildPointsOfInterest (worldBuild.ts:763-798) reads poi.name in one place only, the Wardstone Cairn dialogue userData. The only labels it creates (G.npcList) are for PATHS signposts (line 829-834). The on-screen landmark labels come from a hard-coded LANDMARKS list in overlay.ts:155, which holds the five old landmarks and none of the new places. No test checks the slope at resource node placements. The effect is only visual and the node is still usable, so the severity is low.

confirmed.title: A Three Kettle Camp tent is built on top of a goblin spawn point
confirmed.evidence: The tent piece is at (13 + 2.6, 8 + 2.8) = (15.6, 10.8). The goblin member at line 183 is at (15, 11), 0.63 units away, and the tent's canvas cone has radius 1.6 (buildTent). Probe output: `piece on monster three_kettle_camp tent 15.6 10.8 three_kettle 15 11`. The derived Millrace Road signpost at (12.95, 4.85) is also only 1.3 from the goblin at (12, 4).
confirmed.scenario: On load and on every respawn this goblin appears inside the tent mesh. The player can only click it through the canvas.
confirmed.fix: Move the tent piece (for example dx 3.4, dz 4.2) or the goblin (for example (16, 13.5)) so they are at least 2 units apart. Add a world-data assertion that no POI piece is within 2 of a camp member.

check.reason: Confirmed. buildPointsOfInterest (src/engine/worldBuild.ts:762-771) places each piece at poi.x+dx, poi.z+dz with no rotation, so the second tent stands at (15.6, 10.8). spawnAllResourcesAndMonsters (src/engine/spawns.ts:217-219) spawns the goblin at exactly its member coordinate (15, 11), 0.63 units from the tent centre. buildTent draws a 4-sided ConeGeometry of radius 1.6 (about 1.13 to a flat side) that is 2.0 tall, so the goblin's spawn point is inside the tent mesh. One part of the scenario is wrong: the tent is not in G.worldInteractiveObjects, and the click raycast in input.ts tests only that list, so the tent never blocks clicks. The goblin can still be clicked, but it is hidden or clipped inside the tent geometry at spawn and on every respawn at home. The fault is cosmetic and readability only, so severity stays low. I confirmed that the signpost position is derived from the path's first point with a halfWidth+1 offset, but I did not compute it. A gap of 1.3 is a minor visual crowding issue, not an overlap.

confirmed.title: README world table puts resources in the wrong regions
confirmed.evidence: The Lumbridge row lists "Normal/Oak/Willow Trees". NODE_PLACEMENTS has normal, oak and maple trees in Lumbridge; the willows are at (64, -32) and (70, -38), in Varrock, whose row does not list them. The Varrock row says "Copper & Iron Quarry", but the copper rocks are at (-18, -22) and (-12, -25) in Lumbridge, and Varrock's rocks are iron and mithril. The Korok Woods row lists the lobster and shark spots, which are on the river at x 24-27, z -36..-62, about 100 units from the woods centre. These rows were rewritten in this stage (W8, whose acceptance check is every row against the data) and the errors were kept.
confirmed.scenario: A player follows the table to Lumbridge for willows, to Varrock for copper, or to the Korok Woods for lobster and shark, and finds none there.
confirmed.fix: Lumbridge: Normal/Oak/Maple trees and copper rocks. Varrock: willow trees and the iron and mithril quarry. Move the lobster and shark spots to the river (Lumbridge south) in the table.

check.reason: I could not refute the finding. The code confirms all three errors. In src/data/placements.ts, Lumbridge has normal, oak and maple trees (lines 15-25) and its only rocks are copper, at (-18,-22) and (-12,-25), lines 31-32. The willows are at (64,-32) and (70,-38), lines 40-41, under the Varrock section header. Varrock's rocks are iron and mithril, lines 35-39. The region circles in WORLD_REGIONS (src/data/catalog.ts:430-436) agree. Lumbridge is centred at (0,0) with radius 46, so both copper rocks are inside it (about 28 units out) and the willows are not (about 72 units out). Varrock is centred at (78,-20) with radius 44, and the willows are about 18 units from its centre. The lobster and shark spots, at (24..27, -36..-62) on lines 58-61, are about 99-104 units from the Korok Woods centre at (-75,-30), well outside its radius of 45. They sit only in the data file's Korok section. The first lobster spot falls inside Lumbridge's circle, and the sharks fall inside no region. The README rows at lines 73, 74 and 76 still say Willow in Lumbridge, Copper in Varrock and Lobster & Shark in the Korok Woods. These wrong items were already in the table before W8, but the W8 commit (6c58426) rewrote those exact rows and kept them. So the player scenario does happen. Severity stays low, because only the documentation is wrong: the game itself places and plays these resources correctly.

confirmed.title: G2.7 relocation tests cannot tell a real relocation from the fallback to the start town
confirmed.evidence: expectLoadsWalkable only asserts isWalkable(pose.x, pose.z). sanitizePose (src/state/save.ts:208-229) searches rings out to radius 12 (24 steps x 0.5) and otherwise returns { x: 0, z: 4 }, and (0, 4) is walkable. The ridge coreHalfWidth is 11 (src/data/worldMap.ts:89), so the ring search has only about 1 unit of margin. I bundled sanitizePose and ran it on every blocked point of a 0.5 grid over +/-118 (24,156 points): none fell back to (0, 4) today, and a flood fill showed every walkable cell in one component. The code is correct today. The test is the weak part.
confirmed.scenario: A later data change widens the ridge core past 12 (for example coreHalfWidth 13) or adds a wider basin. A version-4 save standing on the crest then loads in the start town at (0, 4) instead of next to where it was saved. All of the 'loads to a walkable point' cases still pass, because (0, 4) is walkable.
confirmed.fix: In expectLoadsWalkable, also assert that the loaded pose is near the saved one, for example Math.hypot(pose.x - x, pose.z - z) <= ridge.coreHalfWidth + 1 for the ridge case and <= b.radius for the basins. Or assert that the pose is not (0, 4).

check.reason: I confirmed this from the code. expectLoadsWalkable (tests/save-relocation.test.ts:18-22) only checks that the loaded pose is non-null and that isWalkable(pose.x, pose.z) holds. It never checks that the pose stays near the saved point. sanitizePose (src/state/save.ts:208-229) searches 24 rings of 0.5 out to radius 12. If no ring finds walkable ground, it returns { x: 0, z: 4 }, which is walkable start-town ground, so every relocation case would still pass on the fallback. No test in tests/save*.test.ts checks the distance or rejects (0, 4). Harrowback Ridge has coreHalfWidth 11 (src/data/worldMap.ts:89), so a crest point sits about 11 from the nearest walkable ground and the search has about 1 unit to spare. If the core is widened past 12 or a larger basin is added, saves on the crest would silently load in the start town and the tests would stay green. The code works today and the failure needs a future data change, so this is a missing test check rather than a runtime defect: low severity. The fix is to assert hypot(pose - saved) <= 12, or that the pose is not (0, 4), for the ridge, basin and spawn cases.

confirmed.title: G2.9 budget test counts table segments, not segment-distance evaluations per height call
confirmed.evidence: Design G2.9 asks for 'at most 60 segment-distance evaluations per call'. The test sums points.length - 1 over PATHS and RIDGES (22 today). getTerrainHeight (src/state/terrain.ts) calls settledHeight(x, z), then calls settledHeight(poi.x, poi.z) again for every POI pad in range. Each composed() call walks every path and ridge segment. So a call inside a pad costs 22 x (1 + pads in range) evaluations. I measured at most 1 pad in range on a 0.5 grid, which gives 44 today, so the budget holds now.
confirmed.scenario: Tables grow to 31-60 segments, or two pads (plus their 2-unit shoulders) come to overlap. A height call then makes 62-180 segment-distance evaluations and the world-budget test still passes, so the G2.9 bound is no longer proven.
confirmed.fix: Count the real per-call cost: segments x (1 + the largest number of pads whose padRadius + 2 covers one point, computed from POIS) <= 60. Or instrument nearestOnPolyline with a counter and assert the worst case over a grid.

check.reason:
The mechanics are confirmed in the code. In src/state/terrain.ts:21-31, getTerrainHeight calls settledHeight(x,z) once. It then calls settledHeight(poi.x, poi.z) again for every POI pad within padRadius + PAD_SHOULDER (2). Each settledHeight call that is not inside a region core runs composed(), and composed() calls nearestOnPolyline over every PATHS and RIDGES polyline, so it walks every table segment. A call inside one pad therefore costs 2 x table segments: 44 today, against the 22 the test counts. The test at tests/world-budget.test.ts:8-14 only sums points.length - 1 and checks the sum is at most 60. If the tables grew to 31-60 segments, a call inside a pad would cost 62-120 evaluations and the test would still pass. The finding is right about this, and the 22 vs 44 gap exists even today.

The finding does overreach in two places, and there is one mitigating point.
1. The design's own G2.9 row says "at most 60 segment-distance evaluations per call (counted from the tables)". So the test does exactly what the spec says to count. The real defect is that the spec's counting rule is a weak stand-in for the per-call bound in section 8, not that the test departs from the spec.
2. Pads cannot overlap today. The closest pair, Wardstone Cairn (-8,50, r2) and Cinderstep Pass (-19,55, r3), are about 12.1 apart. Their reach is 4 + 5 = 9, so 1 + 1 pad is the current worst case, and the budget holds now.
3. The impact is small even if the bound is broken: about 120 point-to-segment distances per call at fewer than 100 calls per frame is negligible.

So it is a real gap in proving G2.9 but has no runtime effect. Severity: low.

confirmed.title: The 3-second aggression grace after load, teleport and respawn has no automated proof
confirmed.evidence: The 'does not acquire during the 3-second grace' test passes playerSafe: t < 3 directly to stepMonster. Its comment says 'The engine folds the 3-second grace ... into playerSafe'. The real grace lives only in the engine: G.aggroGraceUntil = performance.now() + 3000 at src/engine/session.ts:38 (load), src/engine/actions.ts:47 (teleport) and actions.ts:368 (respawn), read as f.now < G.aggroGraceUntil at src/engine/loop.ts:562. No test reads those lines. The test is the same as the safe-zone case below it.
confirmed.scenario: Someone deletes the grace assignment in loadGameState, changes 3000 to 300, or drops the '|| f.now < G.aggroGraceUntil' term. A version-4 save standing inside a camp that is now aggressive (for example the giants camp at (77.5, 21) r13, or the pass camp after relocation from the ridge) is attacked on the first frame. The whole suite stays green.
confirmed.fix: Move the grace into a pure helper (for example isPlayerSafe(x, z, now, graceUntil) plus a GRACE_MS = 3000 constant in src/state). Test it at now = graceUntil - 1 and graceUntil + 1, and have loop.ts, session.ts and actions.ts call it. Or list the grace under G-4 manual verification explicitly.

check.reason: Confirmed. The grace is set to performance.now() + 3000 in three places: src/engine/session.ts:38, src/engine/actions.ts:47 and src/engine/actions.ts:368. It is read in one place, src/engine/loop.ts:562 (playerSafe = isInSafeZone(...) || f.now < G.aggroGraceUntil). No file under tests/ mentions aggroGraceUntil, imports engine/session, engine/loop or engine/actions, or checks the 3000 ms value. The only grace test is in tests/monster-territory.test.ts, around line 381. It builds the grace itself as playerSafe: t < 3 and passes that to stepMonster, so all it shows is that stepMonster stays idle while playerSafe is true. The safe-zone loop right after it checks the same thing. gate-simulation.test.ts passes only isInSafeZone, with no grace. So removing any of the three assignments, changing 3000, or dropping the '|| f.now < G.aggroGraceUntil' term would leave the suite green, as the finding says. The finding is a test-coverage gap, not a runtime defect: the engine behaves correctly today. If the grace did regress, a player who loads, teleports or respawns inside an aggressive camp would be attacked at once. That annoys the player but is recoverable, so low severity is right.
